cards.b: A compound containing hydrogen and carbon only.
Coal, natural gas and petroleum. Natural gas is mainly methane.
A mixture of hydrocarbons, separated by fractional distillation.
Heated, vapours rise up a column that is hotter at the bottom; fractions condense at different heights by boiling point.
Refinery gas: heating/cooking. Petrol: cars. Naphtha: chemical feedstock. Diesel: diesel engines. Bitumen: roads.

cards.f: Trend from bottom to top of column
cards.b: Chain length decreases, boiling point decreases.
Saturated: only C–C single bonds. Unsaturated: at least one C=C double bond.
Saturated hydrocarbons, single covalent bonds; unreactive except for combustion. Names end -ane.
Unsaturated hydrocarbons with a C=C double bond. Names end -ene.
Shake with aqueous bromine: alkene decolourises it (orange to colourless); alkane does not.
Large alkane molecules broken down with high temperature and a catalyst to give alkenes and hydrogen.
With bromine; with hydrogen (nickel catalyst) to give ethane; with steam (acid catalyst) to give ethanol.
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Ethanol used as a solvent and as a fuel.
Polymer: large molecule built from many small monomers.
Addition: monomers contain C=C, polymer only product. Condensation: two functional groups per monomer; small molecule (water) also formed.

short.q: Describe how petroleum is separated into fractions. [3]
short.model: Petroleum is heated and vaporised; vapours rise up a column that is hotter at the bottom; each fraction condenses at a level where its boiling point matches.
points: fractions condense at different heights by boiling point

short.q: Describe a test to distinguish ethane from ethene. [2]
short.model: Shake each with aqueous bromine; ethene turns it from orange to colourless; ethane does not.

short.q: Describe cracking and give one reason it is carried out. [3]
short.model: Long alkane molecules are broken into shorter alkanes and alkenes using high temperature and a catalyst; used to make alkenes for polymers or petrol.

short.q: Draw or describe the formation of poly(ethene) from ethene. [3]
short.model: Many ethene molecules join as the C=C double bond opens; n CH₂=CH₂ → (–CH₂–CH₂–)n.

short.q: State two differences between addition and condensation polymerisation. [2]
short.model: Addition monomers contain C=C and only the polymer forms; condensation monomers have two functional groups and a small molecule such as water is also formed.
points: only polymer vs polymer plus small molecule
